summary: T6 implementation correctly hardens the OAuth surface (redirect_uri allowlist + RFC 6749 §4.1.3 / RFC 7636 §4.4 binding) and adds the bootstrap-ticket capability flow (LRU+TTL, atomic consume, per-user cap, UUIDv4 capability auth) per Decisions 5 and 7. No critical or high findings. The hand-rolled loopback parser correctly rejects 0.0.0.0, literal `localhost`, lookalike hosts (`127.0.0.1.evil.com`), suffix-bearing paths, non-numeric ports, and missing ports. Loopback acceptance is gated to `client_id == "mnemonic-cli"` and explicitly tested against cursor / claude / vscode / empty. Bootstrap tickets use `Uuid::new_v4()` (122-bit CSPRNG) — unguessable. `BootstrapInner::consume` removes-and-returns under a single tokio mutex guard with no `.await` while held — atomicity verified by `test_bootstrap_ticket_atomic_consume`. The 4th issue per `jwt_sub` returns 429. TTL eviction tested via `force_expire`. Redeem endpoint exempted from `bearer_auth_middleware` via path-prefix allowlist `/api/cli-bootstrap/redeem/`; issue endpoint runs through the middleware and depends on `Extension(Claims)` injection (proven middleware-extracted, not body-derived). No tracing / log statements introduced in api.rs or oauth.rs — A09 (logging-of-sensitive-values) inherently satisfied for this diff.
files_audited: mcp/src/oauth.rs (allowed_redirect, is_loopback_callback, IssuedCode.redirect_uri binding, token_handler equality check, bearer_auth_middleware allowlist update)
mcp/src/api.rs (BootstrapTickets, BootstrapTicket, bootstrap_issue_handler, bootstrap_redeem_handler, bootstrap_not_found, tests)

findings.title: No explicit unit test asserts `http://localhost:<port>/callback` is rejected
findings.description: The `is_loopback_callback` helper only matches `http://127.0.0.1:` or `http://[::1]:` byte-prefixes, so the literal `http://localhost:1234/callback` correctly returns false. The reviewer-supplied focus list called this out explicitly, but no test asserts the negative. The implementation is correct today — this is a regression-prevention gap, not an exploitable bug.
findings.impact: If a future refactor (e.g., adding hostname-aware matching or pulling in a `url` crate parser) accidentally accepts `localhost`, an attacker controlling DNS for `localhost.<their-domain>` (in unusual setups) could exploit. Currently inert.
findings.recommendation: Add one assertion to `test_oauth_allowed_redirect_exact_and_prefix` (or a new test): `assert!(!allowed_redirect("http://localhost:1234/callback", "mnemonic-cli"));` Then add a comment near `is_loopback_callback` explaining the intentional IP-literal-only policy.

findings.title: `redirect_uri` on `/oauth/token` is `Option<String>`; mismatch is rejected only when present
findings.description: The token-handler treats `redirect_uri` as optional `Option<String>` for backward compatibility (legacy webapp client never sent it). RFC 6749 §4.1.3 requires that if `redirect_uri` was supplied at /authorize then it MUST be supplied at /token. As implemented, the equality check is only run when the client supplies the field — an attacker who steals a code can therefore exchange it WITHOUT supplying any `redirect_uri` and the binding check is skipped. PKCE verifier check still gates the exchange, so this is not directly exploitable today (the attacker would also need the verifier), but it weakens defense-in-depth.
findings.impact: Reduces RFC 6749 §4.1.3 mitigation strength against code-injection. Code stays single-use (popped from LRU before any check), so a successful exchange still consumes the code; this is not a code-replay vector.
findings.recommendation: Already noted as a follow-up in `decisions.md` § Concerns 3. Acceptable for Phase 1; track as backlog. Future hardening: when `client_id == "mnemonic-cli"`, require `redirect_uri` on /token (Option::None → 400). Decisions.md captures this — leaving it in backlog is acceptable.

findings.title: Cross-user LRU eviction allows a passive DoS by 100 distinct attackers
findings.description: Production caps are LRU=100, per-user=3. 34 distinct authenticated attackers each issuing 3 tickets (102 tickets total) will saturate the LRU, evicting one legitimate user's ticket per fresh issue. Per-user cap prevents single-attacker amplification, but the LRU is shared. Eviction returns 410-Gone-equivalent (404 — uniform), so legitimate users see a transient failure that is recoverable by re-issuing. No data leak.
findings.impact: Bounded annoyance, recoverable via retry. Risk note in tech-spec § Risks already documents this.
findings.recommendation: Already documented in tech-spec § Risks ("raise the cap or move to Redis"). No code change needed for Phase 1.

findings.title: `dec_user` after `lru.push` has a tautological `peek().is_some()` clause
findings.description: The condition `if guard.lru.peek(&ticket_id).is_some() || evicted.jwt_sub != jwt_sub { dec_user(...) }` is effectively always-true after a successful `push`, since `peek(ticket_id)` returns Some for the just-inserted entry (UUIDv4 collision is a non-event). The OR clause is dead. Code is correct; the comment explains the defensiveness, but the redundancy can confuse a future maintainer into thinking there's a code path where `dec_user` is skipped.
findings.recommendation: Optional cleanup: simplify to `guard.dec_user(&evicted.jwt_sub);` unconditional. Drop the OR clause and the comment about it being defensive. Not required for security correctness.

findings.title: No cross-user keypair leak vector — confirmed by design
findings.description: Reviewed scenario: a malicious authenticated user (Alice) calls /issue with a keypair_json of her choice (could be garbage, could be Bob's keypair if she somehow obtained it). Server stores it under `jwt_sub=Alice` and returns `ticket_id`. Alice could only redeem it herself or share it. The keypair returned at /redeem is whatever Alice POSTed at /issue — there is no way for Alice to redeem a ticket bound to Bob (because Bob's tickets have different UUIDs which Alice cannot guess: `Uuid::new_v4()` is 122-bit random). The /issue endpoint cannot be used to overwrite an existing ticket (UUID is freshly minted server-side, not client-supplied). Per-user cap is enforced before insert. Confirmed no cross-user pollution path.

rationale: All critical security properties from the task spec are implemented and tested. The single coverage gap (T6-SEC-001, literal `localhost` test) is a defense-in-depth nit, not an exploit vector — the implementation correctly rejects it today. The hand-rolled loopback parser is conservative and well-tested. Bootstrap-ticket flow is correctly minimal (no logging, capability-via-UUID, atomic consume, uniform 404). RFC 6749 §4.1.3 binding is in place with a documented Phase-1 allowance for missing `redirect_uri` on /token (mitigated by PKCE verifier check). No CRITICAL or HIGH findings; one LOW (test gap), one LOW (option-not-required redirect_uri), three INFORMATIONAL.
